title: Trilce: Poem LXXVII - It Hails So Much, Enough for Me to Remember
text:
It hails so much, enough for me to remember

and increase the pearls

I have gathered from the very snout

of every storm.


Let this rain not dry up.

Unless I were granted

to fall now for it, or they buried me

wet in the water

that would spring from all fires.


How far will this rain reach me?

I fear some flank of mine will remain dry;

I fear it will go away without having tested me

in the droughts of incredible vocal cords,

through which,

to give harmony,

one must always climb-never descend!

Do we not perhaps climb downward?


Sing, rain, on the coast still without sea!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's reversals: rain from fire, climbing downward, and a coast without sea.

title: Trilce: Poem VII - I Took My Course Uneventfully Along the Veined Street
text:
I took my course uneventfully along the veined street

I know by heart. Everything uneventful,

truly. And I anchored toward things like that,

and I was past.


I turned down the street through which one rarely

passes safely, heroic exit

through the wound of that

living corner, nothing by halves.


These are the largenesses,

that cry, the clarity of confrontation,

the submerged crowbar in its function of now!


When the street is dark-eyed with doors,

and proclaims from barefoot lecterns

to after-morning the salvos in the doubles.


Now minute-making ants

enter, sweetened, drowsed, barely

ready, and they grow crippled,

burned powders, high ones of 1921.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's neologistic street movement, including the strange after-morning and 1921 ending.

title: Trilce: Poem LXIII - Daybreak Comes Raining. Well Combed
text:
Daybreak comes raining. Well combed,

the morning drips its fine hair.

Melancholy is tied up;

and in badly asphalted oxident of Hindu furniture,

fate turns, barely settles.


Skies of heartbroken puna

from great love, the platinum skies, grim

with impossible.


The flock ruminates and underlines itself

with an Andean neigh.


I remember myself. But enough

are the antlers of the wind, the rudders still until

becoming one,

and the cricket of tedium and the hunchback's unbreakable elbow.


Enough the morning of free loose manes

of precious pitch, mountain-born,

when I go out and look for eleven

and they are only twelve unhours.
editorial_note: The translation preserves 'oxident' and 'unhours' to keep the poem's invented temporal/weather language.

title: Trilce: Poem LVII - Cratered the Highest Points, the Points
text:
Cratered the highest points, the points

of love, of capital Being, I drink, I fast, I ab-

sorb heroin for sorrow, for the slack

heartbeat and against all correction.


Can I say that they betrayed us? No.

That all were good? Neither. But

there is good will there, without doubt,

and above all, being so.


And what of whoever loves himself greatly! I seek myself

in my own design, which should have been my

work, in vain: nothing managed to be free.


And yet, who is pushing me.

I dare not close the fifth window.

And the role of loving oneself and persisting, beside the

hours and the improper.


And this one and that one.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the broken 'ab-sorb,' capital Being, fifth window, and unresolved pronouns.

title: Trilce: Poem XXI - In an Arteried Car of Vicious Circles
text:
In an arteried car of vicious circles

December returns, how changed,

with its gold in disgrace. Who would have seen it:

December with its 31 broken skins,

                                                poor devil.


I remember it. We had splendor,

mouths ringleted with bad self-importance,

all dragging infinite suspicions.

How could I not remember

the lean Mister Twelve.


I remember it. And today December returns,

how changed, breath smelling of misfortune,

frozen, sniffling humiliation.


And the fearful ostrich,

as though he had loved her, as though he had adored her.

But she has put on all her differences.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the month as a battered figure and preserves the poem's distorted December logic.
